messages:
maria: heads-up — getting repeated P99 latency pages for embeddings-serving in us-west and eu-central. It's spamming oncall, unsure if it's real regression or alert noise. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: @maria paging: embeddings-serving-p99-high (severity: page) — triggered 14 times in last 6m — https://ops.redwood/alerts/embeddings-serving-p99-high
chris: saw it too. I'm looking at the autoscaler logs now. might be a short burst from a bad batch job.
sanjay: I can take the initial investigation. @chris can you post the autoscaler tail?
chris: quick tail: ```
2026-03-15T08:12:01Z scale_loop: desired=10 current=6 pending=4
2026-03-15T08:12:02Z launch: pod/emb-serve-xyz scheduling
2026-03-15T08:12:10Z pod/emb-serve-xyz ready
```
chris: shows rapid scale up, but pods coming up slowly which explains P99 blips.
jen: I'm on call handover in ~20m. if this looks like a transient scale hiccup, can we quiet the pages and handle by note? Paging is interrupting customers.
maria: marking customer impact unknown atm — customers in two regions reported slow responses. Sanjay, define mitigation plan?
sanjay: mitigation: 1) temporary alert squeal: increase threshold for pages from 95th->99.5th for 30m 2) add a dedupe window to avoid >5 pages / 10m 3) create dashboard panel to track scale lag.
aaron: +1 for dedupe window. we should avoid suppressing real incidents though. prefer short-lived change with clear owner.
ops-bot: runbook check — existing runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/embeddings-scale (owner: ops-team). Last edited 2025-11-02.
maria: action: Sanjay will implement temporary alert changes, Chris will add logs/links to the runbook, Jen will own post-incident follow-up during handoff.
sanjay: making change now — patching prometheus rule: ```yaml
- alert: EmbeddingsP99High
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,service,region)) > 1.2
  for: 5m
```
(switching expr to 99.5 and for: 10m for pages)
chris: added logs section to runbook with autoscaler tail snippet + prod link: https://ops.redwood/dashboards/embeddings/scale-lag
incident-bot: alert mutation recorded by ops-automation: EmbeddingsP99High -> severity: page -> severity: notify (temp), dedupe-window: 10m, expires: 1839003068
jen: taking handoff at 08:30 UTC. I'll monitor the dashboard for the next hour and update customers if we see persistent impact.
maria: thanks. Please capture a short post-incident note in the runbook under "Alert tuning rationale" once we restore original thresholds.
jen: copied. quick notes while monitoring: observed 3 noisy back-to-back pages at 08:11-08:13 tied to a large batch request from a partner tenant ID: partner-73. Telemetry shows request size ~12x typical.
aaron: can we add a pre-filter to autoscaler that rate-limits single-tenant bulk jobs? if not, add a routing/priority hint to avoid mass-scaling events.
sanjay: good idea. I'll sketch a mitigation RFC. For now, post-incident items: 1) revert temp alert changes at expiry 2) add dedupe+cooldown to pager config 3) create a dashboard with "scale-lag vs incoming-batch-size" 4) add runbook annotation with real example request id and a short snippet on how to triage.
chris: assigning ownership in runbook: Alerts section -> owner: chris (alert rules), ops-team (runbook), eng-runtime (autoscaler).
jen: update: no more pages in last 18m, latency trending to normal. I'll mark customer impact: minor (no data loss, slower 2-3s).
maria: excellent. Postmortem? Small blameless note + alert tuning entry is enough. keep it short.
sanjay: created incident note and opened PR to runbook: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/embeddings/PR-457 — includes change log, alert rule diff, and owner tags.
ops-bot: PR linked to runbook audit log.
jen: before handoff ends, I'm adding a short playbook snippet under "On-call handoffs" to make explicit: - when muting alerts set expiry - add handoff owner - note customer impact level + link to alert mutation.
maria: sounds good. Closing thread: we'll revert temp alert at 1839003068 unless we see new pages. If someone wants to keep it longer, comment here and assign owner. :white_check_mark:
